title: POC scoping: integration adapters, SDKs, and structured output (Hightide Freight)
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria, workload shape, benchmark plan, and integration approach. Customer wants OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool/function calling for inventory checks, structured JSON outputs for downstream systems, and clear perf/cost SLOs. Discussed batch sizing, KV cache reuse, quantization tradeoffs, and timeline for a 4-week pilot.
next_steps: Redwood to send POC statement of work and pricing estimate (Maya)
SE team to produce benchmark harness template and expected metrics (Ethan)
Customer to share sample workload traces and schema for structured output (Samira)
Schedule technical kickoff for pilot week of 2027-12-13 (Maya/Carlos)
action_items: Maya Chen: send draft SOW and pricing by 2027-12-03
Ethan Park: provide benchmark harness repo + runbook by 2027-12-06
Samira Patel: deliver sample prompts, 3 months of request traces and output schema by 2027-12-02
Carlos Mejia: confirm VPC/networking constraints and KMS requirements by 2027-12-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-11-30 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Noah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samira Patel (Hightide Head of AI), Carlos Mejia (Platform Eng), Olivia Turner (PM), Ben Holt (Architect)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
Customer is evaluating Redwood for a 4-week pilot to replace current prototype that is slow at scale. Need OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool calling for inventory and ETA checks, and structured JSON outputs for their orchestration layer. Concerned about cost and on-prem data residency.

---

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a sec, i see folks popping in, good morning afternoon depending where you are
00:12 Samira Patel: good morning, thanks for setting this up, excited to get into the details today
00:18 Ethan Park: hey Samira, quick one — we'll focus technical scope and then map out benchmarks and timeline, sound good?
00:25 Carlos Mejia: yup, that works. we have 3 key constraints: regional data residency for eu clients, KMS integration for keys, and we want predictable token/unit costs.
00:37 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll go through how Redwood Dedicated or Private can address residency and KMS, and then talk about pilot success criteria.

02:03 Olivia Turner: quick context — we're running a prototype that calls a mix of OpenAI endpoints and a homegrown reranker. Biggest pain is inconsistent latency and the JSON we get back needs too much post-processing.
02:22 Ben Holt: also we need function/tool calling to check inventory and call our ETA microservice, ideally synchronous so our order pipeline doesn't stall.

03:10 Ethan Park: makes sense. for the pilot we usually recommend 3 things: 1) define success criteria (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy / quality gates), 2) run workload-shaped benchmarks to show steady-state cost+latency, 3) integration plan for SDKs and tool calling.
03:34 Samira Patel: can you give an example of success numbers we might aim for?
03:40 Ethan Park: yeah — typical retail/logistics baseline we aim for is p95 generation latency under 400-500ms for a 256-token response on a hosted optimized model; for Dedicated/private numbers may be lower but depends on batch and quantization. cost target — we'd model to beat current per-interaction spend by ~20% after batching/caching. quality — regression tests on our prompt set with acceptance threshold of 95% parity with your prototype outputs.

05:20 Carlos Mejia: okay batching and caching — can you explain how that will interact with our per-customer isolation? we can't share KV cache across tenants.
05:35 Ethan Park: absolutely. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching with tenancy boundaries: cache scope can be per-tenant or per-namespace, so you get the cost benefits without cross-tenant leakage. we'll show the config in the pilot harness.

07:00 Olivia Turner: what about tool/function calling? we need two patterns: synchronous blocking calls to our ETA API and async fire-and-forget for enrichment. both need structured output adherence to a schema so our downstream services don't break.
07:18 Noah Ruiz: technical note — function calling in Redwood mirrors the OpenAI-style function schema, and we also support stronger structured output via declarative output templates. we can enforce required fields and types as part of the response contract.

08:55 Ben Holt: and if the model refuses or hallucinate? we need fallbacks and audit logs.
09:05 Ethan Park: we'll include a fallback policy in the serving layer — either route to a smaller deterministic reranker or return a structured error. audit and trace logs are captured, with token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.

10:40 Samira Patel: sample workload: we expect 120 requests/sec peak during weekdays, avg 45 req/s, payloads average 200 tokens in prompt and 180 tokens in generation. can you size pods for that?
10:58 Ethan Park: good, that workload gives us a starting point. for 120 rps with 180-token generations, continuous-batching can reduce per-token cost by batching across requests. We'll propose a Dedicated config with autoscaling to handle peaks and burst. initial bench plan: run synthetic replay from your traces and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost per 1k tokens across model variants and quant configs.

12:30 Carlos Mejia: what's the expected duration to get benchmarks running and results? we have a tight timeline — pilot needs to start by mid-december and run for 4 weeks.
12:43 Maya Chen: timeline is tight but doable. proposed schedule:
- this week: Redwood shares SOW and bench harness (Maya/Ethan)
- week of Dec 6: customer provides traces and schema (Samira)
- week of Dec 13: technical kickoff and environment prep (networking/VPC checks)
- week of Dec 13-20: run initial benchmarks and integration tests
- week of Dec 20-27: iterate on tuning and finalize acceptance criteria
- Jan first week: pilot closes and review results

14:05 Olivia Turner: can we run the benchmarks in our VPC? we need data to not leave our control.
14:14 Ethan Park: yes — Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and we can deploy the inference nodes in your VPC. there is some setup effort for peering and KMS, which we'll capture in the SOW.

15:30 Ben Holt: security — we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and bring-your-own-key. are those baked in?
15:45 Maya Chen: yes, we support SOC2 compliance, SAML SSO, RBAC and KMS integrations for Private deployments. We'll attach our security pack and a questionnaire to the SOW.

17:00 Samira Patel: about structured output — our orchestration expects a JSON payload like {order_id, items: [{sku, qty}], eta_minutes: int, confidence: float}. can you guarantee schema enforcement?
17:19 Noah Ruiz: we can enforce schema via function definitions and post-validators. we also support structured output formats where the model is constrained to emit a strict JSON block; if there's deviation we can trigger a deterministic fallback. there will be edge cases, but the regression harness will include prompts that test these fields.

19:05 Carlos Mejia: benchmark metrics — besides latency and cost, what else will you report?
19:12 Ethan Park: we'll report throughput, token-level cost, batch utilization, KV cache hit-rate, tool invocation success-rate, function-call latency, error rates, and quality regressions versus your golden prompt set.

21:30 Samira Patel: any advice on prompts to reduce hallucinations? we currently see 3-5% of responses with incorrect ETAs.
21:42 Noah Ruiz: structured prompts, stronger tool constraints, and a reranker after the model are useful. We can also run a small fine-tuning or RLHF-like alignment on your dataset if needed, but that's heavier. For the pilot we'll focus on prompt engineering + function calling and a deterministic validator for ETAs.

23:10 Maya Chen: on cost modeling — we'll provide an estimated cost model with sensitivity to batch sizes and quantization. could you share an example of current monthly spend?
23:24 Samira Patel: ballpark $18k/month on the prototype, with spikes.
23:30 Ethan Park: goal will be to reduce unit cost and keep or improve latency. we'll show a model that predicts savings at your workload shape.

25:00 Olivia Turner: SDKs — we want something that matches our existing OpenAI wrapper. how close is Redwood SDK?
25:12 Ethan Park: Redwood provides first-class OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs in Python/Node/Go. most customers can swap 2-3 lines of code for parity. we also expose extra headers for tracing and cost attribution. For function calling, the behavior mirrors OpenAI's schema but we add structured output validators and richer error codes.

27:10 Ben Holt: any broken pieces we should expect during the initial swap? we want to avoid a big refactor.
27:20 Ethan Park: usually the biggest work is mapping tool/function calls to your microservice contracts and ensuring schema match. we'll provide an adapter layer in the SDK to translate your function signatures. also small changes in retry logic and streaming behavior may need minor client changes.

29:40 Samira Patel: benchmarks — can Redwood run side-by-side against our current provider? we want apples-to-apples.
29:52 Maya Chen: yes, we can run A/B benchmarks using your replay traces. we'll run the same prompt set against both endpoints and provide token-by-token cost and latency comparisons.

31:10 Carlos Mejia: network egress and VPC — we need clarity on encryption in transit and at rest.
31:20 Ethan Park: all data in transit is TLS 1.2+, at rest is encrypted and in Private deployments keys can be in your KMS (BYOK).

33:00 Olivia Turner: acceptance criteria — let's capture concrete numbers: p95 generation < 500ms for 256 tokens, KV cache hit-rate > 60% after warm-up, function-call success-rate > 99%, per interaction cost <= $X (TBD after redwood sends model estimates), and quality parity >= 95% on the prompt set.
33:28 Maya Chen: sounds good — we'll draft these into the SOW as the acceptance gates.

35:40 Ben Holt: what about fallbacks on capacity problems? if Dedicated nodes saturate, do you have routing to hosted or a smaller model?
35:52 Ethan Park: yes routing policies can fallback to a lighter model or to a degraded mode that returns cached or truncated answers. we can set thresholds for automatic fallback to protect latency SLOs.

37:10 Samira Patel: any blockers from your side we should know about?
37:16 Maya Chen: nothing immediate, but we will need the traces, schema, and network contacts to move fast. The SOW will call out network setup tasks.

39:45 Carlos Mejia: timings for SSO and audit access — will that be part of the pilot or only for production?
39:55 Maya Chen: basic SSO and RBAC can be enabled in pilot for testing; full enterprise audit retention may be part of the production package but we can enable short-term logs for pilot review.

41:08 Olivia Turner: ok let's recap the next steps
41:12 Maya Chen: recap: Maya sends SOW + security pack, Ethan sends benchmark harness and runbook, Samira shares traces and schema, Carlos confirms network constraints, schedule kickoff week of Dec 13th.

42:05 Samira Patel: agreed. can we get pricing options for both Dedicated and Private? we need to compare.
42:14 Maya Chen: yes — we'll include both in the SOW with estimated costs and a recommended configuration for your workload.

44:00 Ben Holt: last question — can we test function calling reliability (1000 invocations/min) in the bench?
44:08 Ethan Park: yes we'll add a stress test for function calls and measure latency and error rates.

46:30 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed dates. appreciate the time.
46:40 Samira Patel: thank you, bye
46:45 Meeting end
notes: Customer will prioritize data residency and BYOK for pilot
Pilot target start week of Dec 13, 2027
Benchmark harness will be replay-based using customer traces
